after.en: Softmax turns scores into nonnegative weights that sum to 1 for any number of classes. The weights can be used as class probabilities, but their reliability still needs calibration and evaluation.

t.en: The sorting machine needs to recognise X, O and + parts. From a camera image, the network first gives each class a score and then decides which kind it is.
Choosing one of three, the network first gives each class a score. But scores can be positive or negative and do not add up to 1, so they cannot be read as "how sure" directly.

Training a classifier also needs a measure of how wrong a prediction is. Cross-entropy, a common choice, looks at the probability assigned to the correct class: the lower that probability, the larger the loss. The game trainer uses squared error, a different loss.

With many classes, we can check whether the top prediction is correct (top-1) or whether the correct class is among the top five (top-5). If the answer ranks second, top-1 counts it wrong and top-5 counts it right; they answer different questions.
In <level-ref to="4-18"></level-ref> you handled two scores. This time the Softmax part is temporarily put aside: build the conversion of three scores to probabilities yourself.

brief.en: The sorting machine has to put parts into three classes: X, O and +. The network first gives each class a score: S1, S2 and S3 correspond to X, O and +. Scores may be positive or negative. Turn the three scores into three probabilities, each between 0 and 1, adding up to 1, with a higher score getting a higher probability. The expected output uses e^score ÷ the sum of the three e^score.

hint.en: Scores can be negative, so dividing by their sum goes wrong. exp turns any number positive.
